review.evidence_summary: Both Open Library records have the same title, author key, and first-publish year, and each has a high-confidence SAME assertion to the same accepted Wikidata identity Q2895947. The packet provides no evidence of a translation, adaptation, collection, or other distinct-work relation.
Both Open Library records have the same author key and first-publish year, differ only in title capitalization, and each has a high-confidence SAME assertion to Wikidata Q1978467.

Both Open Library records have the identical title, author key, first-publish year, and subjects. Each also has a direct high-quality SAME assertion to the same Goodreads entity, with exact author-name and full-work-title matches.

Both Open Library records have the identical title "Kim," the same author key, the same first-publish year (1901), and strongly overlapping subjects. Each is also directly matched by high-confidence pipeline assertions to the same Goodreads entity, with exact author-name and full-title matches.

Both Open Library records have the same author key and 1894 first-publish year, with only capitalization differing between “Bayou folk” and “Bayou Folk.” Each also has a direct high-confidence SAME assertion to Wikidata Q19070339.

All four Open Library records have the same title, author key, first-publish year, and subjects. Each also has a high-confidence SAME assertion to the same Wikidata entity, with no conflicting or split evidence in the packet.

Both Open Library records have the same title apart from capitalization and the same author key. Each also has direct SAME assertions to the same Goodreads entity via high-quality full-title/exact-author matching and to the same Wikidata entity via high-confidence judgments. The differing first_publish_year values do not outweigh this direct convergence.

Both Open Library records have the identical title and author key, and each is directly matched to the same Goodreads entity by AUTO_MATCH_HIGH assertions and to the same Wikidata entity by high-confidence LLM judgments. The one-year first-publication difference does not outweigh this direct convergence.

Both Open Library records have the same author, effectively identical titles differing only in capitalization, closely aligned subjects, and separate high-confidence SAME assertions to Wikidata Q125805927. The differing first_publish_year values (1928 and 1948) do not outweigh this direct convergence.

Both Open Library records have the same title and author key, and each has direct SAME assertions to the same Goodreads entity via AUTO_MATCH_HIGH exact-author/full-title matches and to the same Wikidata entity via high-confidence judgments. The differing first-publish years are not sufficient to establish distinct works.

All three Open Library records have the exact title "Peter Abelard," the same author key, and direct AUTO_MATCH_HIGH identity assertions to the same Goodreads work based on full-title and exact-author matches. The 1933/1944 first-publish-year difference does not outweigh this convergence.

All six Open Library records have the same author key, effectively identical titles differing only in capitalization, and closely aligned subjects. Each also has direct SAME assertions to the same Goodreads entity via high-quality full-title/exact-author matching and direct high-confidence SAME assertions to the same Wikidata entity.

Both Open Library records have the identical title, first publication year, and subjects, and each has a high-confidence SAME assertion to the same Wikidata entity. The differing Open Library author keys indicate an authorship-attribution variant rather than a distinct work.

Both Open Library records have the same title apart from capitalization, closely aligned subject coverage, and adjacent first-publish years. Each has a direct AUTO_MATCH_HIGH Goodreads identity assertion based on WORK_FULL title matching and EXACT_NAME author matching to the same Goodreads entity; the differing OL author keys therefore appear to be attribution-record variation rather than evidence of distinct works.

Both Open Library records have the identical title and first-publication year, share author OL284540A, and independently have high-quality direct SAME assertions to Goodreads entity E000039142 based on full-title and exact-author-name matches. The extra author keys on E000012608 are best represented as an attribution variation between duplicate records.

Both Open Library records have the identical title, share author OL215741A, have closely aligned first-publish years (1887 and 1886), and substantially overlapping subjects. Each also has a high-confidence SAME assertion to Wikidata Q124086571; the additional author on E000022262 is consistent with an authorship-attribution variant.

All three Open Library records have the same full title, closely aligned 1914–1915 publication years, and overlapping Royal Navy fiction subjects. Each also has a direct AUTO_MATCH_HIGH Goodreads identity assertion based on BOOK_FULL title matching and EXACT_NAME author matching to the same external entity. The differing Open Library author keys are consistent with duplicate author attribution records rather than distinct works.

All 16 Open Library records have the identical title, all are directly matched by high-status Goodreads pipeline assertions to the same Goodreads entity, and 15 share closely aligned subject metadata. Most use the same author key; the remaining author-key differences are accompanied by exact or compatible author-name matches. The varying first-publish years are consistent with duplicated edition-derived work records but prevent a high-confidence determination.

Both Open Library records have the same 1925 first-publish year, share author OL117A, and each has a high-confidence SAME assertion to the accepted Wikidata identity Q5704466. The titles and secondary author attribution differ, so the common conceptual identity is supported but not directly asserted between the two OL records.

Both Open Library records have the same author key and variant titles, “Old New Land (Altneuland)” and “Altneuland.” Each is directly matched to the same Goodreads entity by high-quality automated matches and to the same Wikidata entity by high-confidence judgments. The differing first-publish years do not outweigh this direct convergence.

Both Open Library records have the same author and near-identical titles differing only by the initial article “Die.” Each is directly matched to the same Goodreads entity with exact author-name and full title/work matching, and independently to the same Wikidata entity with high-confidence MATCH decisions. The differing first-publish years do not outweigh these direct identity assertions.

All three Open Library records have the same author and high-confidence SAME assertions to Wikidata Q464928. E000006719 and E000006829 additionally share the same title, first-publication year, subjects, and high-quality Goodreads match to the same entity, supporting duplicate status. E000002099 uses a different-language title, while its subjects include translations into English, supporting a translated title variant of the same conceptual work.

All three Open Library records have the same author key, closely matching titles, and overlapping Blue Beard subjects. Each also has a direct high-confidence SAME assertion to Wikidata Q161138; E000018774 additionally has a high-quality Goodreads match.

All 19 Open Library records have high-confidence direct SAME assertions to Wikidata Q840974. They also share the same principal author, closely aligned subjects, and titles limited to “Ivanhoe,” “Scott's Ivanhoe,” and “Sir Walter Scott's Ivanhoe”; two records merely add coauthor attributions.

The Open Library records have different titles and first-publish years: “Scaramouche” (1921) and “Scaramouche the king-maker” (1931). Each also has a high-quality direct match to a different Goodreads entity, while both converge on one Wikidata entity. This supports treating the Wikidata convergence as an overmerge rather than collapsing the two OL targets.

The OL records have different titles and first-publish years and each matches a different Goodreads entity, while both are asserted to match the same Wikidata entity. The packet does not clarify whether this reflects duplicate works, a part/collection relationship, or Wikidata over-aggregation, so identity cannot be resolved safely.

Both Open Library records share the distinctive title “St. Ives,” the same primary author, and closely overlapping subjects; the longer title appears to add a subtitle. Both also have direct high-quality Goodreads matches to the same entity. Their separate high-confidence Wikidata matches and differing additional author attributions create an external-source conflict, but the supplied Open Library metadata supports treating them as duplicate records for one conceptual work.

All four Open Library records have the same author key and closely corresponding Russian, transliterated, and English titles. Each also has a direct high-confidence SAME assertion to Wikidata Q75840; Goodreads independently links three records through two accepted identities. The differing Goodreads targets do not provide explicit evidence of distinct conceptual works.

The records form two title families: “The tales of Jacob”/“Die Geschichten Jaakobs” and “Joseph und seine Brüder”/“Joseph and his brothers.” The latter pair shares direct Goodreads identity and separate Wikidata support. Wikidata Q3829111 links both the Jacob-title pair and the English Joseph record, conflicting with the distinct Q282181 identity for the German Joseph record and indicating likely external over-aggregation.

All eight Open Library records have the same primary author, closely aligned titles and subjects, and direct SAME assertions to Wikidata Q880092; seven assertions are high-confidence and one is medium-confidence. The expanded title on E000020406 and additional author attributions on E000007154 and E000020627 are consistent with title and authorship variants. Goodreads uses two identities for two records, creating a source-level split but no packet evidence of distinct conceptual works.
